summary: Control exact ordinary Aico widgets and retained owner roots, create roots, and observe or administer pinned roots.

help:
Usage: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --project PROJECT --project-root PATH [--resume-session SESSION_ID] [--surface aico|a-term]
       st aico widget status|title|position [OPTIONS]
       st aico root status|show|title|position|end REQUEST_ID [OPTIONS]
       st aico roots [REQUEST_ID] [--watch SECONDS]
       st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] [OPTIONS]

create: one exact owner root with transient sanitized prompt; optional native Codex resume in a newly allocated root. roots: compact verified identity and advisory TUI status; bounded watch. admin: pinned request; currently fails closed because native atomic idle/draft/thread control is unavailable. widget/root: exact owner view controls and root end. Output contains metadata only. Receipts: applied:false means nothing was applied; applied:null means unknown, so reconcile with status before any retry.

Native message delivery remains sessions send/verify: exact UUID + stable source revision; queued/durable does not prove consumption or slash execution.
help.create:
Usage: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --project PROJECT --project-root PATH [OPTIONS]

--resume-session SESSION_ID resumes an exact saved native session in a new owner root; no picker, latest-thread inference or terminal input. Default --tool codex, --surface aico, --role portfolio-root. Use --surface a-term for the existing loopback owner HTTP route (configured authentication remains enforced). --lead-root and --facet are optional opaque metadata. PROMPT or --stdin supplies <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes; no secrets or framing controls. Resume without either uses a fixed post-crash reconciliation prompt. Fresh create requires a prompt.

Reuse the same REQUEST_ID and complete body after an uncertain response. Matching retries reconcile the same root; changed body conflicts; ended requests remain tombstones. Output is bounded content-free metadata. No prompt retention or fleet ledger; sessions emit/wait apply only to fleet-started roots. Creation requires an already running owner; Aico shows its new root, A-Term creates a detached pane. --root-socket PATH selects Aico's private GUI socket; --root-url URL selects A-Term's loopback HTTP owner. No deployment or owner startup.
help.roots:
Usage: st aico roots [REQUEST_ID] [--watch SECONDS] [--interval SECONDS]

Omit REQUEST_ID to discover running catalog roots. An exact ID can also report a retained unavailable root. Snapshot JSON contains identity/status only; --watch (>0, <=3600 seconds) emits baselines and changed states only. Poll interval defaults to 2 seconds (minimum 0.1). Discovery is bounded to 128 catalog entries and 256 KiB; snapshots have a 10-second bound. Identity races fail closed and watches never re-pin. Unknown/unsupported TUI profiles are ambiguous/unavailable. GUI/owner absence is unavailable; this command never starts Aico.

Native-thread delivery is separate: exact bound UUID + stable --source-key revision, <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes. Passive default. A queued/durable receipt does not prove working/consumption and has no process-generation fence. Terminal admin capability is exposed separately by admin; execution currently fails closed.
help.admin:
Usage: st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] [OPTIONS]

Omit the operation to inspect the owner capability. clear/submit require --generation SHA256 --thread UUID --request-key KEY. submit also requires --stdin (<=2000 UTF-8 bytes; no framing controls). Reuse the same request key after an uncertain response.

Currently fails closed: native atomic current-thread + idle/empty-draft/input fence and idempotent receipt are unavailable. Returns concise content-free metadata; never sends tmux input, captures text, retries Enter, or changes permissions. An uncertain transport reports applied:null. --root-socket PATH selects an exact private owner socket.
help.widget:
Usage: st aico widget status [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]
       st aico widget title "Name" [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]
       st aico widget position X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Control one exact ordinary Aico widget before using desktop automation. Omit --widget-id to use the exact AICO_WIDGET_ID from this managed pane; missing or invalid identity fails closed. IDs require 8 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Each mutation reads the exact widget immediately first, sends its current generation, and verifies the returned identity and generation. No fleet/root discovery or native-thread inference. GUI absence is unavailable; this command never starts Aico. Output contains identity/status metadata only, never label content. applied:false means a qualified refusal or no request; applied:null means the outcome is unknown; reconcile with status and never blindly retry.
help.widget status:
Usage: st aico widget status [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Read one exact ordinary widget descriptor through the private GUI socket. Defaults to this managed pane's AICO_WIDGET_ID; an explicit --widget-id selects only that exact 8-character lowercase hexadecimal ID. Missing/invalid identity fails closed. Output contains owner/widget/session/generation/status/availability metadata only.
help.widget title:
Usage: st aico widget title "Name" [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Rename the exact ordinary widget using its immediately read current generation. Defaults to AICO_WIDGET_ID; no selection or thread inference. Supply a non-secret control-free single-line label of 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes. Content goes only to the owner's existing session metadata; receipts and errors contain no label. Missing, unavailable or stale generations fail closed.
help.widget position:
Usage: st aico widget position X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [--widget-id ID] [--root-socket PATH]

Arrange the exact ordinary widget using its immediately read current generation. Defaults to AICO_WIDGET_ID. Bounds are integers with absolute values at most 100000; width >=360 and height >=240. Missing, unavailable or stale generations fail closed. No desktop capture/input or owner startup.
help.root:
Usage: st aico root status REQUEST_ID [--surface aico|a-term]
       st aico root show REQUEST_ID [OPTIONS]
       st aico root title REQUEST_ID "Name" [OPTIONS]
       st aico root position REQUEST_ID X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [OPTIONS]
       st aico root end REQUEST_ID [OPTIONS]

Control one exact retained owner root (direct st aico create or fleet-started) by request ID. Mutations read the exact descriptor first, require running status, pin its generation, send one request and verify identity and generation in the receipt. Non-running roots fail closed. --surface aico (default) uses the private GUI socket (--root-socket); a-term uses its loopback owner route (--root-url) and supports status/show/title/end. No fleet event, prompt or label retention; never starts an owner. For fleet roots prefer sessions close so the fleet ledger records End.
help.root status:
Usage: st aico root status REQUEST_ID [--surface aico|a-term] [--root-socket PATH | --root-url URL]

Read one exact retained root descriptor: owner, request, host and logical identity, surface locator, generation and status (running, pending, uncertain or ended). No terminal or label content.
help.root show:
Usage: st aico root show REQUEST_ID [--surface aico|a-term] [--root-socket PATH | --root-url URL]

Show or reopen the exact running root's view using its immediately read generation. Non-running, ended or changed roots fail closed. No desktop capture/input.
help.root title:
Usage: st aico root title REQUEST_ID "Name" [--surface aico|a-term] [--root-socket PATH | --root-url URL]

Rename the exact running root using its immediately read generation. Supply a non-secret control-free single-line label of 1-160 trimmed UTF-8 bytes. Content goes only to the owner's existing session metadata; receipts and errors contain no label. st sessions title is a compatibility alias.
help.root position:
Usage: st aico root position REQUEST_ID X Y WIDTH HEIGHT [--root-socket PATH]

Arrange the exact running Aico root using its immediately read generation. Bounds are integers with absolute values at most 100000; width >=360 and height >=240. A-Term positioning is unavailable.
help.root end:
Usage: st aico root end REQUEST_ID [--surface aico|a-term] [--root-socket PATH] [--owner-socket PATH | --root-url URL]

End the exact root's workload with its immediately read generation. Aico uses the headless owner End containment contract (--owner-socket, default AICO_CONTROL_SOCKET) and accepts only an exact ended receipt; A-Term uses its root end route. An ended tombstone reports applied:false and sends nothing. Blocked cleanup or lost transport reports applied:null: reconcile with root status, never relaunch. Fleet roots: prefer st sessions close.

usage.cmd: st aico create REQUEST_ID [PROMPT] --project PROJECT --project-root PATH [--resume-session SESSION_ID] [--surface aico|a-term]
usage.when: create a new owner root or explicitly recover one exact saved Codex thread after a crash
precautions: Owner adapter validates the native ID; only Codex with a lowercase UUID is implemented. New root launch; never paste into an existing pane or choose latest/picker entries.

Prompt is transient, sanitized and bounded to 2000 UTF-8 bytes. No secrets, transcript or fleet ledger. sessions emit/wait apply only to fleet-started roots. Default recovery prompt reconciles state before continuation.
Reuse request ID and full body on retry; conflicts fail closed, ended roots remain tombstones. Running proves workload presence, not authenticated model readiness or prompt completion.

usage.when: read compact identity/status for existing Aico catalog roots or watch bounded status changes
precautions: Read-only; no terminal/draft text. One-time verified owner/server/pane discovery; identity races fail closed and watches never re-pin.
Visible TUI status is advisory, not objective completion. Unknown profiles are ambiguous/unavailable; GUI/owner absence is unavailable.

Instruction delivery uses sessions send separately: passive default; native-thread requires exact UUID + stable revision and <=2000 sanitized UTF-8 bytes. Queued/durable does not mean working/consumed and is not generation-fenced.

usage.cmd: st aico admin REQUEST_ID [clear|submit] --generation SHA256 --thread UUID --request-key KEY [--stdin]
usage.when: inspect or request Aico-owned native terminal administration at an idle scope seam
precautions: Currently fail-closed; the native atomic thread/idle/draft/input operation and idempotent receipt are unavailable.
No terminal input/capture or retry. Text enters only bounded stdin; output is content-free. Reuse the same request key after an uncertain transport.
